claims.text: The proposed model combines DFT-derived interatomic force constants with explicit anharmonic lattice-dynamics simulations.
The model can predict lattice thermal conductivity independently of electronic thermal conductivity.
Below approximately 200 K, the lattice thermal conductivity follows a T^3 temperature dependence.
Below approximately 200 K, the predicted lattice conductivity is about 20% higher than conventional Debye- or elasticity-based estimates.
At 300–1200 K, the model enables separation of the electronic contribution from the lattice contribution.
After accounting for 1 wt.% oxygen and independently adding the electronic contribution, predicted total conductivity will fall in the measured range of 10–17 W/(K·m).
The modeled specimens are nearly defect-free and have minimal extrinsic scattering.
HfNbTaTiZr can form a metastable single β-BCC phase upon quenching or an α-HCP plus β-BCC dual-phase structure upon slow cooling.
Printed and sintered equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen have been produced.
Full phonon dispersion and anharmonic scattering determine the relevant temperature-dependent vibrational properties.
Capturing atomic-mass variation, force-constant variation, and anharmonic interactions permits separation of phonon-mediated heat transport from electronic transport.
Previous Debye- and elasticity-based approaches inherently conflate lattice and electronic conductivity.
The proposed approach reduces uncertainty by approximately 10–20% relative to earlier methods.
Earlier analytical approaches deviate from measured conductivity by as much as ±25%.
The model is expected to be robust from approximately 50 K to 1200 K for nearly defect-free bulk HfNbTaTiZr with controlled oxygen content.
Below 50 K or above 1200 K, phase instabilities or additional scattering mechanisms may reduce model accuracy.
Hall-effect or thermopower measurements can independently determine the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution for the proposed comparison.
